quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: Feeling good and pleased about something.
Feeling unhappy, often because something bad happened.
Needing to rest or sleep because you have little energy.

quests.hint: Think about how each word describes a different feeling.
quests.explanation: Happy means you feel good, sad means you feel unhappy, and tired means you need rest. Each word describes a different feeling a person can have.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.
The meal eaten in the middle of the day.
The main meal eaten in the evening.

quests.hint: Think about the order these meals happen during a day.
quests.explanation: Breakfast comes first in the morning, lunch happens in the middle of the day, and dinner is the evening meal. Knowing these words helps you talk about your daily meals.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A woman who has a child.
A man who has a child.
A girl or woman who has the same parents as you.

quests.hint: Think about who belongs to your family and how they are related to you.
quests.explanation: Mother and father are your parents, and a sister is a female child of the same parents. These are basic family words used every day.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A set of printed pages with a cover that you read.
A thin tool used for writing or drawing.
A piece of furniture you sit on.

quests.hint: Think about common objects you might find in a classroom.
quests.explanation: A book is for reading, a pencil is for writing, and a chair is for sitting. These are simple classroom objects every student uses.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: To move quickly using your legs.
To move by putting one foot in front of the other slowly.
To push yourself off the ground into the air.

quests.hint: Think about how each word describes a different way of moving your body.
quests.explanation: Run is fast leg movement, walk is slower and steady, and jump means pushing off the ground. Each verb describes a different physical action.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A person trained to treat sick people.
A person whose job is to help students learn.
A person who controls and steers a vehicle.

quests.hint: Think about what job each person does for other people.
quests.explanation: A doctor helps sick people get better, a teacher helps students learn, and a driver controls a car or bus. Each word names a different job.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A piece of clothing worn on the upper body.
Items worn to cover and protect your feet.
A piece of clothing worn on your head.

quests.hint: Think about which part of the body each clothing item covers.
quests.explanation: A shirt covers the body, shoes cover the feet, and a hat covers the head. Each word names clothing for a different body part.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: Having a high temperature.
Having a low temperature.
Having a temperature that feels pleasant, not hot or cold.

quests.hint: Think about temperature, from very high to mild to very low.
quests.explanation: Hot means very high temperature, cold means very low temperature, and warm is a gentle, pleasant temperature in between. These words describe how something feels.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A large vehicle that carries many passengers on roads.
A vehicle that travels on tracks, often carrying many people.
A two-wheeled vehicle you pedal with your feet.

quests.hint: Think about different ways people travel from place to place.
quests.explanation: A bus and a train both carry many passengers, while a bicycle is powered by pedaling. Each word names a different way to travel.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: The room in a house where food is cooked.
The room in a house where a person sleeps.
The room in a house used for washing and using the toilet.

quests.hint: Think about what each room in a house is mainly used for.
quests.explanation: The kitchen is for cooking, the bedroom is for sleeping, and the bathroom is for washing. Each word names a room with its own clear purpose.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: To move something so it is no longer closed.
To move something so it covers an opening.
To use force to move something away from you.

quests.hint: Think about actions you do with doors and other objects every day.
quests.explanation: Open means making something not closed, close means shutting it, and push means moving something away using force. These are common action words.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: The first day of the work week in many countries.
A weekend day that comes after Friday.
The current day, right now.

quests.hint: Think about how each word relates to time and the days of the week.
quests.explanation: Monday starts the work week, Saturday is a weekend day, and today means the present day. These words help you talk about when things happen.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A round fruit with red, green, or yellow skin.
A baked food made from flour and water.
A white liquid produced by cows, used as a drink.

quests.hint: Think about common foods you might buy at a grocery store.
quests.explanation: An apple is a fruit, bread is baked from flour, and milk is a drink from cows. Each word names a different everyday food item.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: To get something by paying money for it.
To give something to someone in exchange for money.
To give money for something you want.

quests.hint: Think about the actions people do when they are shopping.
quests.explanation: Buy means getting something with money, sell means giving something for money, and pay means handing over money. These words describe different sides of a shopping action.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: Large in size.
Little in size.
Having a great height.

quests.hint: Think about words that describe the size of an object or person.
quests.explanation: Big describes something large overall, small describes something little, and tall describes height specifically. These adjectives describe size in different ways.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A common pet animal that barks.
A common pet animal that meows.
An animal with feathers that can usually fly.

quests.hint: Think about the sounds and features of different animals.
quests.explanation: A dog barks, a cat meows, and a bird usually has feathers and can fly. Each word names a different type of animal.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: To look at written words and understand their meaning.
To make letters or words on paper using a pen or pencil.
To pay attention to sounds in order to hear them.

quests.hint: Think about the different skills you use when learning a language.
quests.explanation: Read means understanding written words, write means putting words on paper, and listen means paying attention to sound. These are all important language skills.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: Water that falls from clouds in drops.
Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky.
Air that moves quickly outside.

quests.hint: Think about different kinds of weather you might see outside.
quests.explanation: Rain falls as drops of water, snow falls as frozen flakes, and wind is moving air. Each word names a different type of weather.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: To curve your mouth upward to show happiness.
To produce tears, often because of sadness or pain.
To make sounds that show you find something funny.

quests.hint: Think about how each word shows a different feeling on a person's face.
quests.explanation: A smile shows happiness, crying shows sadness or pain, and laughing shows something is funny. Each word describes a different facial expression or reaction.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A place where you go to see a doctor for a check-up.
A shop where you can buy medicine.
A large building where sick or injured people receive treatment.

quests.hint: Think about different places connected to health and medicine.
quests.explanation: A doctor's office is for check-ups, a pharmacy sells medicine, and a hospital treats sick or injured people. Each place serves a different health need.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A sport played by kicking a ball into a goal.
Moving through water using your arms and legs.
Moving your body to music in a rhythmic way.

quests.hint: Think about different physical activities people enjoy for fun or exercise.
quests.explanation: Soccer involves kicking a ball, swimming involves moving through water, and dancing involves moving to music. Each word names a different physical activity.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A device used to make calls and send messages.
An electronic device used for working, browsing, and storing information.
A device used to watch shows and programs.

quests.hint: Think about different electronic devices people use at home.
quests.explanation: A phone is for calls and messages, a computer is for work and browsing, and a television is for watching shows. Each word names a different everyday device.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: Happening or arriving before the expected time.
Happening or arriving after the expected time.
In a short time from now.

quests.hint: Think about words that describe when something happens compared to an expected time.
quests.explanation: Early means before the expected time, late means after it, and soon means a short time from now. These words help you talk about timing.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: An opening in a wall, usually covered with glass, that lets in light.
An opening used to enter or leave a room or building.
The covering on top of a building.

quests.hint: Think about different parts of a building and what each one does.
quests.explanation: A window lets light in, a door lets people enter or leave, and a roof covers the top of a building. Each word names a different part of a building.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A person you know well and like spending time with.
A person who lives near you.
A person you do not know.

quests.hint: Think about how close or distant your relationship is with each kind of person.
quests.explanation: A friend is someone you like and know well, a neighbor lives nearby, and a stranger is someone you do not know at all. Each word describes a different kind of relationship.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: The early part of the day, before noon.
The part of the day between noon and evening.
The part of the day when it is dark, used for sleeping.

quests.hint: Think about the order these parts of the day happen, from sunrise to sunset.
quests.explanation: Morning is the early part of the day, afternoon comes after noon, and night is the dark time used for sleeping. These words divide the day into parts.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: Costing very little money.
Costing a lot of money.
Costing no money at all.

quests.hint: Think about how much money you would need to pay for something.
quests.explanation: Cheap means it costs little, expensive means it costs a lot, and free means it costs nothing. These words describe price from low to high.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: A place where airplanes take off and land, and passengers board.
A place where trains or buses stop for passengers.
A building where travelers pay to sleep for one or more nights.

quests.hint: Think about different places connected to traveling away from home.
quests.explanation: An airport is for airplanes, a station is for trains or buses, and a hotel is where travelers sleep. Each word names a different travel-related place.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: To start doing something.
To complete or stop doing something.
To keep doing something without stopping.

quests.hint: Think about the different stages of doing an activity, from start to end.
quests.explanation: Begin means to start, finish means to complete, and continue means to keep going. These words describe different stages of an activity.

quests.instruction: Match the words with their meanings.

pairs.value: Making very little or no noise.
Making a lot of noise.
Making no sound at all.

quests.hint: Think about how much sound or noise each word describes.
quests.explanation: Quiet means very little noise, loud means a lot of noise, and silent means no noise at all. These words describe sound from none to a lot.
